chunks: 134 - From him, from Saʿd, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, from Abī Maryam, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام went out, along with ʿAbdullāh and ʿUbaydullāh, the two sons of al-ʿAbbās, and ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar; and with them was a son of al-Ḥasan عليه السلام called ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. He died at al-Abwāʾ while he was in ihram, so they washed him, shrouded him, did not apply ḥanūṭ to him, covered his face and head, and buried him.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, said: The one killed in the way of Allah before the Imam of the Muslims, if he dies immediately, then no ghusl is required for him, and he is buried in the garments in which he was killed. From those garments, the trousers are removed, unless blood has reached them, in which case they are not removed from him and are buried with him. Likewise, the fur garment and the cap are removed from him; but if blood has reached them, they are buried with him. The khuff is removed from him in every circumstance. If he does not die immediately, but remains alive and then dies afterward, he is washed, shrouded, and perfumed with ḥanūṭ. And every slain person other than the one we have mentioned, whether unjust or wronged, is to be washed, shrouded, perfumed with ḥanūṭ, and then buried.

key_terms.الْمَقْتُولُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: one slain in the path of Allah
key_terms.غُسْلٌ: the ritual washing required for the deceased
key_terms.فَغَسَّلُوهُ: they performed the ritual washing of the deceased upon him
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: a person in the state of ihram
key_terms.يُحَنِّطُوهُ: they applied or did not apply funeral perfume (ḥanūṭ)

ai.seo_question: What are the rulings on washing and burying a muhrim and a martyr in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report narrates the burial of a muhrim from the family of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام and then states legal rulings concerning the washing and burial of those killed in the way of Allah. It distinguishes between the martyr who dies immediately in battle before the Imam of the Muslims and other slain persons, setting out when ghusl, shrouding, and ḥanūṭ are required.
